# Crayon book recipe

Concept: a single picture-book page in wax crayon on toothy paper, shot with one camera and no cuts. The hero draws itself in. Story words sit on scraps of blank paper. A watercolour wash crosses the page in bands, turns it to night, and exposes what was drawn in white wax from the start: stars, lamps, a message. The last move is a slow push onto the hero, name printed underneath.

## What the page is
The page is finished in front of the viewer. Warm off-white paper, a small box of crayons, child-logic perspective (gable front with a slanted side wall, people taller than doors, faces on the moon and on objects), colour that runs over the outline, lines that boil because each frame is a new drawing. Drawing and colouring are the plot: colouring in a lamp is the lamp coming on, and night falling is paint. Tone: tender, unhurried, a few short lines that read like the book's printed text.

Behaviour of the material makes the look, not a filter. Wax lands only on the peaks of the paper tooth, and pressure sets how deep it gets. Watercolour darkens bare paper and slides off wax. So crayon colours stay bright at night and white wax appears out of nowhere.

Rule out:
- cute vector art with a crayon texture laid on top
- a whiteboard explainer (no hand, no marker)
- a watercolour painting (the wash is the guest, crayon is the host)
- a chalkboard
- a slideshow: one page, one camera, no cuts, no dissolves

## Paper, wax, line
Paper: `--latar`, warm off-white. The tooth is fixed to the page, built from value noise at 1.35, 2.9 and 6.3 px, a horizontal fibre term (10 x 1.9 px), and faint grooves. Contrast `smoothstep(.16, .86)`. Emboss from one side, weaker where wax has filled the tooth (x (1 - .55 * wax)). Mottle +-2%. Warm vignette 0.3: corners lose about 25% and go amber.

Wax adhesion (the central rule): paint each crayon layer with alpha = pressure, then keep wax only where `tooth > 1 − 1.22·pressure`, soft edge +-.07. Light pressure leaves speckle on the peaks. Heavy pressure is nearly solid and 10% darker.

Line: a ribbon with slow hand wobble (1.7 px), width +-15%, ends tapering over 25% of the stroke (cap 28 px), a denser core at half width, one or two thin streaks. Widths at 1920 wide:
- buildings and hero: 6.5-7 px
- characters: 6 px
- faces and details: 4-5 px
- roof tiles, strings, spars: 3-4 px

Colouring: zig-zag hatching joined into long strokes. Row gap about 9 px, stroke about 10 px. Vary each pass between 0.72 and 1.14x pressure so single strokes show. Overshoot the outline by up to 6 px. Large areas add a lighter cross-hatch (+1.25 rad, 45-70% pressure). Small spots (cheeks, pupils, lamps) get tight round scribbles.

Watercolour: a single wash split into three horizontal bands that alternate direction.
- Edges wavy, +-10 px, on top and bottom.
- Density 0.8; 26 bristle streaks (55% darker, 45% lifted).
- Darker tide line just inside each edge; granulation in the deepest tooth pits; soft blooms.
- It multiplies the page and wax resists it: density x (1 - .93 * coverage).
- Bands overlap by about 75 px so no white stripe survives.

Knock-out: anything drawn after the wash (characters, props) carries paper behind its silhouette, as a child draws the figure first and colours round it. Faces stay legible at night.

Words go on a ragged patch of blank paper (a squarish superellipse with a wavy edge) with the same grain. Never on a dark box.

## Build
No live 3D. At load, paint the page once into two images: day (paper + crayon + emboss + vignette) and night (day x wash), per pixel from a seeded PRNG. Reveal the night band by band through clip paths with a moving front. Line art and characters are small sprites painted three times with different boil seeds, swapped at 12 fps. A 512 px seamless tooth tile keeps the paint under a second.

## Palette
- `--latar`: paper and blank patches. `--teks`: printed words and the hand-lettered title. `--utama-di-latar`: the name on the last patch.
- `--tinta`: every outline, pupil and string. It is the indigo outline crayon `#2d3263` mixed 25% toward `--teks`. Never black. It stays dark on a light fill even when a dark brand makes `--teks` light.
- `--utama`: the hero's crayon (the kite here) and half the roof (`--atap` = 55% roof red + 45% `--utama`). `--aksen`: lamp halos and every other tail bow. `--latar-2`: a second paper, such as a taped card, when needed.
- Fixed crayon box, about a dozen and no more:
  - yellow `#f5c63c` (moon, lit window)
  - orange `#ec8a3c` (craters, cheeks)
  - ochre `#e7b867` (walls)
  - brown `#7a4b31` (chimney, spars, ladder)
  - pink `#ee8ea4`
  - peach `#f4c7a4` (skin)
  - sky `#79acd9`
  - violet `#6a5aa6` (eye bags)
  - green `#62a24c`
  - white wax `--putih` (80% white into `--latar`), nearly invisible on paper until the wash arrives
- Watercolour `--cat`: ultramarine `#1a2c84` plus 8% `--utama`. What shows through the wash is this colour. In the film the night averages `#3f4367` over paper `#d0cbbf`.
- Saturated crayon on plenty of bare paper. Value comes from pressure, not extra hues. Pale brand: white paper, its pale colour still reads through indigo outlines. Dark brand: black construction paper, and white wax plus coloured crayon carry the picture.

## Type
`--font-isi` (the book's printed words): Patrick Hand, 62 px on patches, 52 px for detail lines under a name, in `--teks`. Tilt each glyph +-2.5 degrees, nudge +-3%, mask with the paper tooth so it reads as crayon. Write left to right in 0.4-0.5 s, boiling on twos (+-0.8 px).

`--font-judul` (lettering on the page): Caveat 700.
- 118 px sky title, written at about 0.045 s per letter
- 92 px name on the last patch
- 76 px numbers in the sky
- 210 px for a counted total
- sky lettering is white wax on the night

No brand fonts: Patrick Hand with Caveat; Fredoka 700 for a rounder, younger title.
One phrase per patch, six words at most. A wider brand font wraps to two lines, so pin patches to the bottom and let them grow upward.

## Timing
- Everything drawn runs at 12 fps. Line boil cycles three drawings every 1/12 s (jitter +-0.8 px, wobble +-0.9 px; background lines at 0.6 strength, characters at full). On the final hold it slows to every 1/6 s. Camera and wash front stay smooth.
- Draw-on: hero = six drawings in 0.5 s (outline at a third, two thirds, whole; then colouring and tail at a third, two thirds, whole). Its string takes three. Small props take two (outline, then coloured), 1/6 s apart. No in-betweens: poses and states swap.
- Wash: each band crosses in 1.4 s, power1.inOut, front bulging about 50 px ahead mid-page with a dark wet rim. Bands one and two start 1.6 s apart; hold a breath of about 1.1 s before the third. In the film: 0.7, 2.2 and 5.3 s into a 12 s shot.
- Lamps flash on as yellow scribble halos (two drawings, 1/12 s apart) right after the wash passes. A face changes expression by substitution on the beat.
- Words: letter by letter over 0.35-0.5 s; phrases cut hard; hold each at least 1.8 s.
- Camera: locked wide most of the film. One slow push to 1.4x in 1.15 s (power2.inOut) at the end, then at least 2 s still.
- Nothing fades, since crayon cannot. A title leaves by being washed over (it faintly survives), an object by being coloured over, a scene by the camera moving away.

## Camera
The camera is one transform on the whole page: scale from the top-left corner plus a translation.
- Locked full page, 1x: the material is the motion. Opening drawn in, tableau, list being drawn.
- Held wide while the brush crosses (1.4 s per band): weather, night, a reveal. Hidden feature, white-wax message, before/after.
- Slow push to 1.4x over 1.1-1.3 s, then hold: "this one", a feeling arriving. Name, offer, call to action.
- Tilt along a gaze, 0.8 s: we see what the character sees. Discovery, spotting a problem.
- Slow truck left to right: reading a sequence. Steps, a family, a timeline.
- Pull out past the page edge: the page becomes an object. Book on a table, fridge drawing, thank-you card.
- Page turn: new chapter. Next day, before and after.

## Signature moves
- Wax resist. Set the payoff in white wax from frame one; the wash uncovers it. Stars and kite lamps at a night festival; a product's hidden feature; a teacher's thank-you to the class; a bedtime story's secret ending.
- Drawn live. Outline first, then zig-zag colour, over a handful of 12 fps drawings. A kite rising from a child's hand; a new menu item; chapter one of a course; a creator's mascot waking.
- Colouring is an action. Things happen by being coloured: lamps lit by yellow scribble, a window lit, a coat put on. A town lighting shop by shop; a team pulling on its kit; a plant ripening on a small farm; a student's progress map filling in.
- Child logic. Numbers written in the sky by each item, faces on the moon and on objects, perspective wrong on purpose. Counting kites up to "120"; a launch countdown; a talking house for a renovation service; days until a school trip.
- Printed words on blank paper. Each story line appears letter by letter on a torn patch, a few words at a time. A bedtime story channel; a bakery's promise; a museum's short history; event details under the hero.
- Boil. A held frame stays alive because lines keep being redrawn; slowing the boil settles the ending. A pause before the price; a calm closing card; a moment of thanks.
- It is a book. Pull out until the page lies on a table, or turn the page. A year in review; part two of a series; a class reunion invitation.

## Pitfalls
- Performance: paint paper, crayon and wash once at load into the two images; at runtime only move clip paths and swap small sprites. Never redraw a canvas per frame. Use the seamless tooth tile, not a full-screen noise field. Keep sprite boxes tight and paint time near one second. No blend mode or CSS filter over the page: the multiply is baked into the night image.
- Gaps between bands show as white stripes. Overlap them and let the last band reach below the frame.
- Sky text survives the wash because wax resists. Place a title under a band only after it has been read (over 1.2 s), or print it on a patch.
- Characters vanish under the wash. Draw them after it, on a paper backing. Light-pressure colouring goes muddy under the wash; use pressure 0.8 or higher wherever it will be washed.
- Outlining hair reads as a headband. Outline hair masses on their outer edge only.
- Dark brands: faces and pupils take `--tinta`, not `--teks`, or they vanish into the white eye wax. Check that the night still separates from dark paper via stars and coloured crayon.
- The final push moves props. Plan where each lands at 1.4x so nothing written sits under or beside the closing patch.
- Never dissolve or fade crayon between beats. Never cut to a new page without a page turn.

## Reference numbers
- One continuous 12 s shot, no cuts, motion energy 2.4.
- Palette share: night wash `#3f4367` 60%, paper `#d0cbbf` 19%, ochre walls `#c09450` 11%, washed roof `#855f62` 9%.
- Bands: 0.7 s top, left to right; 2.2 s middle, right to left; 5.3 s bottom, left to right. Each crossing about 1.2 s. Full night from 6.6 s. Push toward the moon from 9.5 s while its face changes.
- Layout: house bottom left (front gable, slanted side wall, red roof with tile arcs, chimney, ladder). Moon upper middle-right, radius about a sixth of frame height. Child on the ridge. About 170 white-wax stars, 40% five-pointed.

# Crayon book: beat plan

Default length 15 s. Tempo per beat (seconds): short 1.8, medium 2.6, long 3.6.

## hook

- en: the page is already drawn; the hero draws itself in live while the question is hand-lettered in the sky
- id: halaman sudah tergambar; tokoh utama digambar langsung sambil pertanyaannya ditulis tangan di langit

## problem

- en: the camera holds wide on what is still bare paper or uncoloured outline; the words print on a paper scrap
- id: kamera diam di bagian yang masih kertas kosong atau garis tanpa warna; kalimatnya tercetak di sobekan kertas

## fact

- en: a watercolour band sweeps across; things drawn in white wax appear as it passes
- id: sapuan cat air melintas; gambar dari lilin putih muncul begitu kuas lewat

## step

- en: one part of the page drawn live per step, outline then zig-zag colouring, a number written beside it
- id: satu bagian halaman digambar tiap langkah, garis dulu lalu arsiran zig-zag, nomornya ditulis di samping

## compare

- en: one page in two halves: left coloured in, right still outline, until the colouring or the wash crosses over
- id: satu halaman dua sisi: kiri sudah diwarnai, kanan masih garis, sampai warna atau cat air menyeberang

## number

- en: child logic: small things drawn one by one with their numbers in the sky, then the total lettered big
- id: logika anak: benda kecil digambar satu per satu dengan angka di langit, lalu totalnya ditulis besar

## proof

- en: the thing is coloured in on its word (lamps lit with yellow scribbles), a short line printed below
- id: bendanya diwarnai tepat pada katanya (lampu menyala jadi coretan kuning), kalimat pendek tercetak di bawah

## offer

- en: the offer printed on a torn paper scrap under the hero, the key word lettered in the brand colour
- id: penawaran tercetak di sobekan kertas di bawah tokoh, kata kuncinya ditulis tangan dengan warna brand

## cta

- en: slow push to the hero; name and contact printed on a paper scrap letter by letter, held 2 s, lines boiling
- id: kamera mendorong pelan ke tokoh; nama dan kontak tercetak di sobekan kertas, diam 2 detik, garis tetap hidup

## payoff

- en: the finished night page held wide, stars twinkling, a last line printed on paper, held 2 s
- id: halaman malam yang sudah jadi, diam lebar, bintang berkelip, kalimat terakhir tercetak, diam 2 detik
